title: Add RAG batch-toolchain playbook and local probing harness
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: teams building retrieval-augmented workflows often need a compact, reproducible toolkit to validate end-to-end behavior under batch ingestion and mixed synchronous/asynchronous tool-calling. This PR adds a lightweight RAG 'batch toolchain' example plus a local prober harness that simulates real-world traffic patterns (parallelized ingest, KV cache warmup, and downstream tool latency) so engineers can iterate on batching, cache policies, and tool timeouts without a full infra stack.

What this PR contains (single string): - new example directory examples/rag-batch-toolchain containing a README, a Docker Compose playground, a TS sample client, and a small Python prober used to drive synthetic load; - playbook.md that documents common tuning knobs (batch_size, max_window, cache_ttl, fallback_model) and recommended observability dashboards to add to the Console; - a local 'prober' (prober/main.py) that exercises: bulk ingestion of documents into a toy vectorstore, repeated RAG queries with configurable inter-request jitter, and simulated tool-calling latencies to exercise the platform's streaming and fallback behavior; - CI doc build step and smoke tests demonstrating end-to-end flow with a tiny model (redwood/local-tiny) so the example runs quickly on dev machines.

Quickstart (excerpt from README, one-line commands): 1) git clone && cd examples/rag-batch-toolchain; 2) ./scripts/setup-local.sh (creates a venv, installs dependencies and a tiny local model image); 3) docker-compose up --build --abort-on-container-exit (starts local toy-store + prober + sample API shim); 4) python3 prober/main.py --profile batch_small --concurrency 8 --requests 200 --tool-latency 120. The README also includes a minimal TS sample client to show how to call the example toolchain via the Redwood SDK.

Compatibility and scope: this is intentionally small and self-contained; it demonstrates batching and tool-chaining tradeoffs without depending on Dedicated or Private features. It references Console dashboards and explains where users should map example metrics to production dashboards.

Checklist: - [x] example code + README - [x] prober harness with configurable profiles - [x] playbook.md with tuning guidance and observability mapping - [x] CI smoke + doc build - [x] reviewed and signed off by SRE and Docs.

Related: ENG-4782 (workshop and lab for performance tuning), PM-219 (example content request). Links: internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4782, sample dashboard template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/RAG+Batch+Playbook.

Notes for maintainers: keep examples small; prober profiles are under examples/rag-batch-toolchain/profiles/*.json and meant to be expanded by contributors. If adding model variants, document expected token/latency tradeoffs in playbook.md.
